title: Jump Game IX
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums`. From index `i` you may jump to index `j` in either of these two cases:

- `j > i` and `nums[j] < nums[i]`: jump to the right onto a **strictly smaller** value.
- `j < i` and `nums[j] > nums[i]`: jump to the left onto a **strictly larger** value.

You may make any number of jumps (including none) and may visit the same index several times. For every index `i`, find the **largest value** `nums[j]` among all indices `j` that can be reached when starting at `i`. Return the answers for all indices.

**Follow-up:** In the interview, the candidate was asked to first describe a brute-force approach (a graph search from every index) and then improve it to the optimised solution.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the maximum reachable value for each index, in order.

examples.explanation: From index 0 (value 2) we can jump right to index 1 (value 1); from index 1 we can only jump back to index 0, so both reach at most 2. Index 2 holds 3: nothing lies to its right and no larger value lies to its left, so it only reaches itself.
Index 0 jumps right to index 2 (1 < 2). From index 2 we can jump left to index 1 (3 > 1), which holds the maximum, so every index can reach the value 3.
Equal values never allow a jump, so each index reaches only itself.

hints: Think of the indices as a graph and ask which indices end up in the same connected group. Brute force: run a search from every index, O(n^2).
The jump rules are symmetric (if you can go from `i` to `j`, you can come back), so reachable sets are connected components, and each component is a contiguous block of indices.

A boundary between positions `i` and `i+1` joins the left and right sides exactly when `max(nums[0..i]) > min(nums[i+1..n-1])`. Compute prefix maxima and suffix minima, then sweep from the right, propagating the answer across joined boundaries.

def gen(rng):
    def fmt(a):
        return str(len(a)) + "\n" + " ".join(map(str, a))
    tests = [
        fmt([2, 1, 3]), fmt([2, 3, 1]), fmt([5, 5, 5]), fmt([7]), fmt([1, 2]), fmt([2, 1]),
        fmt([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), fmt([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]), fmt([3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]),
    ]
    for n in (3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30):
        for hi in (4, 10, 1000):
            tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, hi) for _ in range(n)]))
    N = 100000
    tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, 10**9) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(list(range(1, N + 1))))
    tests.append(fmt(list(range(N, 0, -1))))
    # blocks: values decrease inside a block, blocks increase overall
    blocks, cur = [], 0
    while len(blocks) < N:
        size = rng.randint(1, 300)
        vals = list(range(cur + size, cur, -1))
        rng.shuffle(vals) if rng.random() < 0.3 else None
        blocks += vals
        cur += size
    tests.append(fmt(blocks[:N]))
    tests.append(fmt([rng.randint(1, 3) for _ in range(N)]))
    return tests
